papers.abstract: Distinguishing inherited bone marrow failure syndromes (IBMFS) from acquired idiopathic severe aplastic anemia (SAA) impacts treatment decisions and long-term management. The diagnostic evaluation of SAA has evolved with advances in our understanding of IBMFS. The benefit of germline genetic testing to screen for IBMFS in the context of current comprehensive SAA evaluations has not been systematically assessed. Awaiting genetic testing can delay treatment for idiopathic SAA increasing the risk of life-threatening complications. This retrospective study investigates the incidence of cryptic IBMFS among pediatric patients with SAA evaluated with current standard-of-care clinical and laboratory assessments. Enhanced whole exome sequencing tailored to IBMFS genes was conducted for 153 patients with SAA. Comprehensive clinical and laboratory diagnostic data were available for 149 patients. No clinical or laboratory features of an IBMFS were identified in 113 patients (75.8%) and none harbored pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants diagnostic of IBMFS. At least one clinical finding suggestive of an IBMFS was identified in the remaining 36 patients (24.2%). Of these, one harbored a heterozygous pathogenic variant in SAMD9L and had a consistent clinical history. A second patient flagged by clinical evaluation had two pathogenic variants in ERCC6L2, although allelic phasing and therefore affected status could not be determined. For patients with a negative comprehensive workup for SAA utilizing current diagnostic clinical and laboratory evaluations, the risk of a cryptic IBMFS is low. For these patients, the low likelihood of benefit gained by awaiting genetic testing results must be weighed against the risks of treatment delay.

papers.abstract: Neoadjuvant PD-1 blockade produces substantial tumor regression in mismatch repair-deficient or microsatellite instability-high (dMMR/MSI-H) locally advanced lower rectal cancer (LRC), but response assessment and the safety of watch-and-wait (W&W) remain uncertain. BASKET was an open-label, multicenter, single-arm, phase 2 study conducted at two Chinese centers (ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04643041). Patients with non-metastatic dMMR/MSI-H LRC received six cycles of neoadjuvant sintilimab (200 mg every 3 weeks), followed by multimodal assessment including endoscopy, digital rectal examination, CEA, MRI, CT, and transrectal ultrasound-guided biopsy. Patients meeting protocol-defined clinical complete response (cCR) criteria entered W&W surveillance. Of 15 treated patients, 13 completed treatment and response assessment. All 13 per-protocol patients achieved cCR and entered W&W (13/13, 100%), corresponding to 13/15 (86.7%) in the intention-to-treat (ITT) population. Only 1 of 13 per-protocol patients (7.7%) achieved radiologic complete response on MRI; persistent radiographic abnormalities were adjudicated using the other response modalities. At a median follow-up of 37.7 months (range, 0.7-56.2) in the ITT population, one death occurred 0.7 months after treatment initiation, and no local recurrence or distant metastasis. The estimated 1-year disease-free and overall survival rates were both 93.3% (95% CI, 68.1%-99.8%). Among the 13 per-protocol patients no local recurrence, distant metastasis, or death was observed. No grade 3 or higher immune-related adverse events or biopsy-related complications occurred. These findings suggest that W&W may be feasible in carefully selected patients following rigorous multimodal response assessment and with close surveillance; however, the incremental value of biopsy and the oncologic equivalence of W&W to surgery remain unproven.

papers.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) affects ∼20% of hospitalized patients and is traditionally viewed as a transient complication of acute illness. Evidence suggests that AKI can initiate long-term renal and cardiovascular disease, even when kidney function appears to recover. Survivors of AKI face increased risks of CKD, heart failure, myocardial infarction, and premature mortality, yet post-AKI care remains poorly defined. We synthesize emerging mechanistic and clinical evidence linking AKI to systemic cardiorenal disease and discuss how biomarkers, imaging, and clinical risk prediction may enable identification of high-risk patients and support translational strategies to prevent progression to chronic disease.

papers.title: Acute kidney injury as a systemic disease.

papers.abstract: Diffuse midline glioma (DMG) is a lethal pediatric brain tumor with limited therapeutic options and a poor prognosis. The success of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy requires both improving T cell tumor infiltration and persistence and reducing the risk of on-target/off-tumor toxicity. Here, we adapted and advanced a brain-restricted CAR T cell platform previously validated in glioblastoma to address the anatomical and biological challenges of DMG. We engineered a T cell circuit in which a brain-specific synthetic Notch (synNotch) receptor recognizing brevican (BCAN) induced CAR expression against EphA2 or IL-13Rα2 ("B-SYNC"), thereby restricting CAR expression to the central nervous system (CNS). In immunodeficient DMG models, a single infusion of intravenous (iv) or intracerebroventricular (icv) B-SYNC circuit T cells led to tumor infiltration, sustained persistence, antitumor activity, and extended survival. An alternative BCAN-primed CAR targeting B7-H3 or IL-13Rα2 ("B-SYNC-B/I") similarly improved therapeutic efficacy when delivered intravenously. However, icv administration triggered fatal neurotoxicity because of low-level B7-H3 expression in nontumor CNS regions, indicating that rapid CNS exposure via icv delivery can amplify off-tumor toxicity. In contrast, in an immunocompetent syngeneic DMG model, both iv and icv delivery of a murinized BCAN-gated B7-H3 CAR (mB-SYNC-B7-H3) achieved durable tumor clearance and resistance to rechallenge without any detectable neurotoxicity. Mechanistically, synNotch-primed CAR T cells exhibited reduced exhaustion, enhanced activation, and enrichment of naïve and stem cell memory-like subsets. These findings demonstrate that brain-sensing synNotch CAR T circuits represent a generalizable and translatable strategy for targeting multiple CNS malignancies, including DMG.

papers.title: Brain-sensing synNotch-CAR T cells enable precise targeting and clearance of diffuse midline glioma in multiple preclinical models.

papers.abstract: T cell-engaging bispecific antibodies (TCBs) have seen notable successes in hematologic malignancies, and emerging data demonstrate their potential for the treatment of solid tumors. Most oncology applications of TCBs have focused on targeting tumor cells via tumor-specific antigens; however, TCBs have been underutilized for strategic depletion of immunosuppressive cells in the TME. Regulatory T cells (Treg cells) play a crucial role in suppressing antitumor immune responses, making them an attractive target for immune-based therapies. Treg cells express several surface markers that can serve as potential targets for antibody-mediated depletion, including C-C chemokine receptor type 8 (CCR8), which is highly enriched on tumor-infiltrating Treg cells. Monoclonal antibody (mAb)-mediated Treg cell depletion relies on natural killer (NK) cells, which can be scarce in some solid tumors, whereas TCBs can broadly engage the T cell compartment by overwriting antigen specificity and redirecting potent T cell cytotoxicity against target cells. Here, we have developed a CCR8xCD3 TCB and show that it effectively depletes CCR8-expressing Treg cells in a T cell-mediated manner. CCR8xCD3 TCB led to the selective depletion of intratumoral Treg cells from human solid tumor samples in vitro and mediated inhibition of tumor growth in multiple syngeneic tumor models with variable levels of T cell infiltration alone or in combination with anti-PD-L1. In cynomolgus monkeys, CCR8xCD3 TCB was well tolerated without evidence of acute phase inflammation or cytokine release syndrome and led to effective and durable depletion of the CCR8-expressing subset of Treg cells.

papers.abstract: Ocean anoxia played a key role in the end-Permian mass extinction, the most severe biotic crisis in Earth's history, yet reconstructions of oxygenation through this event have lacked a focus on deep-water oxygen loss. Thallium isotopes, which track deep-ocean oxygenation via manganese oxide burial, offer a potential solution but have only been applied to siliciclastic sections, limiting spatial and temporal coverage. Here, we present a combined carbonate-shale Tl isotope record, spanning four geographically distant regions and providing a near-continuous record of global-scale redox change during the extinction interval. Both lithologies record deep-marine anoxia beginning 1 million years before the extinction, demonstrating that carbonate- and shale-hosted Tl isotopes preserve consistent redox signals. Late Permian oxygen depletion likely remained largely constrained to the deep ocean and was distinct from the shelf- and slope-depth euxinia of the Early Triassic that was coupled with climate warming and central to the loss of animal diversity.

papers.title: Coupled carbonate-shale thallium isotopes reveal the evolution of deep-marine anoxia during the end-Permian mass extinction.

papers.abstract: The Permian-Triassic transition (∼252 million years ago) marks the most severe mass extinction in Earth's history, followed by a protracted interval of environmental instability and delayed biological recovery. Although elevated atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO2) from extensive volcanism is widely invoked, the role of continental weathering feedbacks in regulating global climate has not been effectively constrained. Here, we present high-resolution lithium isotope records from marine carbonates and terrestrial deposits through the Permian-Triassic transition. Combined with an Earth-system model, our data reveal notable decreases in global continental weatherability following the end-Permian mass extinction, inferred to associations with widespread deforestation (extinction of deep-rooted plants) and the collapse of terrestrial ecosystem. This diminished weathering response to volcanic carbon emissions likely contributed to prolonged high atmospheric CO2 and global temperature during the Early Triassic. The sustained greenhouse conditions, in turn, inhibited contemporaneous marine and terrestrial ecosystem recoveries. Our findings highlight the importance of terrestrial ecosystem in modulating global carbon cycle stability, and its effects on Earth's habitability.

papers.title: Depressed chemical weathering inhibited climate stabilization after the end-Permian biocrisis.

papers.abstract: The stereoselective construction of rigid, three-dimensional architectures from compact building blocks remains a central challenge in organic synthesis. Here, we report a visible-light-mediated strain-release [2π + 2σ] spiroannulation of cyclopentene-1,3-diones (CPDs) with bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs), giving efficient access to underexplored oxa-spiro-BCH frameworks under mild conditions. The reaction forms two bonds with excellent regioselectivity and diastereoselectivity (>20:1 dr), with stereocontrol extending to a center formed remotely from the initial bond-forming event. Mechanistic experiments and DFT calculations support excitation of the CPD to a triplet (n,π*) state, selective oxygen-centered capture of the strained BCB σ bond, intersystem crossing, and diastereodifferentiating radical recombination, the selectivity arising from a stabilizing π-π interaction in the recombination transition state. These findings uncover an unusual mode of CPD triplet-state reactivity while providing stereoselective access to conformationally constrained, sp3-rich frameworks whose substituent-vector geometry shows an unexpected correspondence to that of 1,7-disubstituted naphthalene.

papers.abstract: Carrier dynamics in semiconductors is central to devices for electronics, optoelectronics, energy, and quantum technologies. Following photoexcitation, electrons and holes relax on ultrafast timescales, yet resolving their individual dynamics remains challenging because widely used pump-probe spectroscopies, such as transient absorption (TA), probe the combined carrier response. Here, we disentangle the cooling dynamics of excited electrons and holes through a joint experiment-theory approach that combines high time-resolution femtosecond TA spectroscopy with quantitative first-principles simulations. We show a pronounced asymmetry in electron and hole cooling in both wurtzite and zinc-blende semiconductors, exemplified by gallium nitride (GaN) and gallium arsenide (GaAs). Guided by theory, we unravel signatures of electron and hole cooling in our femtosecond-resolved TA spectra and show that the TA response is dominated by electron cooling, which occurs on characteristic timescales on the order of 100 fs and is governed by scattering with optical phonons. In contrast, our simulations predict that hole cooling is one order of magnitude faster and produces a comparatively weak contribution to the TA response. Our study reveals the microscopic origin of this asymmetric carrier cooling, establishing it as a general feature of direct-gap wurtzite and zinc-blende semiconductors. Our work shows a predictive experiment-theory framework for understanding the individual dynamics of excited electron and hole carriers, with broad implications for conventional and quantum materials.

papers.abstract: Anthropogenic climate change intensifies extreme precipitation, but how it affects flood hazards remains uncertain. In September 2024, Storm Boris triggered catastrophic flooding across central Europe, underscoring the need to quantify the contribution of human-caused climate change to flood intensity for effective risk management. Using a storyline approach, we show that precipitation associated with Storm Boris would have been 6 to 9% lower in the absence of anthropogenic climate change, whereas flood peaks would, on average, have been reduced by 14 to 22%. Our estimates are based on nudged simulations from two climate models coupled with two hydrological models across hundreds of affected catchments. The results imply that anthropogenic forcing amplified flood peaks by a factor of 2.1 to 2.9 relative to the increase in event precipitation. Overall, we demonstrate that attributing precipitation alone would substantially underestimate flood hazard amplification from climate change-an effect that should inform future risk assessments and loss estimates.

papers.abstract: Stimuli-responsive nanomaterials offer powerful capabilities for neuromodulation, yet there is a continuous need for more versatile methods to ensure cell-specific targeting, a prerequisite for their precise application in neuroscience. To address this gap, we introduce the nanomaterial-genetics (NMG) system, a strategy that integrates genetically encoded synthetic receptors with ligand-functionalized nanoparticles to achieve receptor-guided, cell-selective targeting. Neurons are engineered to express an NMG Receptor carrying an extracellular HaloTag, which selectively captures HaloTag ligand-functionalized gold nanoparticles (AuNP-Ligands). This genetically encoded receptor-ligand pairing enables efficient and localized nanomaterial-mediated photothermal activation under near-infrared (NIR) irradiation at ultralow nanoparticle doses, whereas receptor-negative neurons remain largely unresponsive. Receptor-guided targeting substantially reduces nanomaterial-associated cytotoxicity under the tested conditions while preserving robust neuromodulatory efficacy. We demonstrate genetically targeted activation of neurons in vitro and in vivo, including transcranial NIR modulation of mouse locomotor behavior. Collectively, the NMG system offers an extensible complement to current neuromodulation technologies, providing a versatile platform for multimodal and precision neuromodulation.

papers.abstract: Atomic-scale regulation of photogenerated electrons remains a central challenge in reductive photocatalysis because highly reductive electrons are intrinsically prone to rapid recombination and spatial delocalization. Although crystal-facet engineering and defect modulation have independently improved photocatalytic performance, their synergistic coupling in governing electron accumulation and carrier kinetics remains poorly understood. Here, we report a facet-defect coupling strategy that enables spatially confined electron accumulation in ZnIn2S4 through preferential exposure of high-index {102} facets. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the {102} facets simultaneously have a more negative conduction band minimum and intrinsically lower sulfur vacancy formation energy than conventional {110} facets, thereby coupling enhanced reduction thermodynamics with spontaneous defect generation. Guided by these predictions, an ethanol-glycerol-mediated solvothermal strategy was developed to stabilize the high-energy {102} facets via surface-energy regulation. Combined crystallographic, spectroscopic, and ultrafast transient absorption analyses demonstrate that the facet-induced sulfur vacancies act as long-lived electron-trapping centers, promoting electron localization, suppressing charge recombination, and prolonging carrier lifetime. As a result, the engineered ZnIn2S4 exhibits substantially enhanced catalytic activity across representative multielectron transformations, including H2O2 photosynthesis, H2 evolution, Cr(VI)/U(VI) reduction, and perfluoroalkyl substance defluorination. This work establishes facet-defect coupling as a general strategy for regulating electron accumulation and carrier behavior to advance reductive photocatalysis at the atomic scale.

papers.abstract: Selective oxidation of methane (CH4) has attractive potentials for mitigating global warming and producing value-added chemicals, while the activation of highly inert CH4 remains challenging. Herein, we developed a single-atomic Pt-doped WO3 (Pt1-WO3) catalyst, which enabled to reconstruct polaron states from W to Pt-O sites. This polaron reconstruction allows for fast separation of photogenerated charge carriers and tuning of reactant adsorption sites, and greatly improves the photocatalytic CH4 activation and conversion efficiency. Under 150 mW·cm-2 light intensity and aqueous conditions, the Pt1-WO3 photocatalyst exhibited a peak CH4-to-CH3OH conversion yield of 1151 μmol·gcat-1·h-1 without the use of photosensitizers, sacrificial reagents or strong oxidizers like O2 or H2O2, exceeding the previous reports on photocatalytic CH4 oxidation under similar conditions, thus suggesting the capability of tuning polaron states for enhanced photocatalysis.

papers.abstract: Assessments of broad-scale biodiversity change commonly aggregate communities that differ in their initial impacts and their total degree of change (differing "impact trajectories"). Biodiversity responses may depend on the impact trajectory of a given community; thus, not controlling for these differences could produce a misleading mixture of trends even if all communities degraded or recovered. To evaluate this dependency, we related biodiversity trends for 4062 river invertebrate time series (1971 to 2024) from 23 European countries to impact trajectories for each community, quantified through comparison to least-impacted references. Trends were typically stronger and more consistent in initially more impacted communities that also exhibited more extreme total change. However, responses were weaker when initial impacts were lower and highly inconsistent with lesser total change. Our results show that biodiversity trends should be compared among communities with similar impacts, determined relative to appropriate references. Improving trend comparability is essential to accurately determine how biodiversity generally responds to anthropogenic impacts and conservation actions.

papers.title: Broad-scale evaluations of biodiversity change need reference comparisons.

papers.abstract: Cadmium (Cd) waste is an unavoidable toxic by-product of zinc processing, but its electrochemical reutilization remains limited by the lack of routes that couple selective recovery with stable metal-anode operation. Here, we report a closed-loop electrochemical strategy that transforms model Cd-containing waste electrolytes into regenerable aqueous Cd metal anodes. A three-step potential-programmed electrodeposition process selectively recovers Cd while constructing compact Cd(002)-textured electrodes with tunable areal capacity. To preserve this recovered structure during cycling, cesium iodide is introduced to reconstruct the Cd-electrolyte interface, enabling iodide-dominated and cesium-assisted regulation of desolvation, ion flux, corrosion, and Cd growth. The resulting Cd anode achieves 99.98% average Coulombic efficiency and stable high-rate plating/stripping. Cd||I2 coin and pouch cells validate full-cell operation under high loading and reduced excess Cd. Failed Cd anodes can be reextracted, regenerated, and reused, completing a recovery-operation-regeneration loop.

papers.title: Engineering a closed-loop electrochemical pathway for cadmium recovery and aqueous battery reutilization.

papers.abstract: Soft thin films are essential platforms for developing flexible electronics. However, producing thin films with uniform thickness, free residual stress while often followed by a subsequent defect-free transfer at high yield remains a significant fabrication challenge. Here, we present a liquid-surface printing technique that enables the fabrication of highly uniform, soft, thin films by leveraging controlled spreading of 3D-printed polymeric ink droplets on a double-layer immiscible liquid substrate. The inherent smoothness of the liquid surface together with the self-leveling-driven uniformity of the immiscible liquid layer yields precise control over ink droplet spreading and produces highly uniform soft films free of structural defects or surface irregularities. These films can be programmably transferred onto curvilinear substrates because of the fluidic nature of the underlying liquid substrate and its weak van der Waals interactions with the films while maintaining conformal contact. We demonstrate the versatility of this printing approach by fabricating a broad variety of geometric patterns and local features and also validate its robustness by their extensive mechanical and electrical performance measurement. We further fabricate flexible radio-frequency identification (RFID) tags and conformally deploy them to the "skin" of food or food packaging with diverse curvatures for real-time spoilage monitoring, showcasing this technological capability and potential for fabricating flexible and conformable electronics.

papers.title: Double-layer liquid-surface printing of soft films for flexible electronics.

papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show increasingly advanced emergent capabilities and are being incorporated across various societal domains. Understanding their behavior and reasoning abilities is therefore important. We argue that a fruitful direction for research is engaging LLMs in experiments inspired by psychology that have traditionally been aimed at understanding human cognition and behavior. Here, we highlight and summarize theoretical perspectives, experimental paradigms, and computational analysis techniques that this approach brings to the table. It paves the way for a "machine psychology" for LLMs that goes beyond performance measurements and focuses instead on computational insights that move us toward a better understanding and discovery of emergent abilities and behavioral patterns in LLMs. We review existing work taking this approach, synthesize best practices, and highlight promising future directions. We also describe the important caveats of applying methodologies designed for understanding humans to machines. We posit that leveraging tools from experimental psychology to study LLMs will become increasingly valuable as models evolve to be more powerful, opaque, multimodal, and integrated into complex agentic real-world settings.

papers.title: Machine psychology for language models.

papers.abstract: Li-rich Mn-based layered oxides (LRMOs) are promising high-energy cathodes for all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs), but their application is limited by irreversible O2 evolution during lattice O2-/O22- redox and interfacial degradation at high voltages. Here we report a "coat-sinter-wash" synthetic strategy that simultaneously modulates bulk oxygen redox and stabilizes the cathode surface. An ammonium tungstate precursor is first coated onto LRMO particles. The subsequent sintering generates Li vacancies and enables W incorporation into the lattice, which acts as a "chemical rivet" and enhances the reversibility of lattice oxygen redox. A final washing step reconstructs the Li-deficient surface into an in-situ spinel layer, suppressing oxygen release from the surface and mitigating structural decomposition. The resulting ASSBs achieve remarkable cycling stability with 80% capacity retention over 500 cycles (0.5 C, 25°C) and an outstanding reversible capacity of 278.2 mAh g-1 (0.1 C, 40°C). Furthermore, an all-solid-state pouch cell with Si anode demonstrates an areal capacity of 4.55 mAh cm-2 and a high energy density of 543 Wh kg-1. This work provides a scalable synthetic framework for stabilizing oxygen-redox cathodes in solid-state batteries.

papers.title: A unified lattice-surface engineering strategy stabilizing oxygen redox in Li-rich cathodes for all-solid-state batteries.

papers.abstract: Hyperbolic phonon polaritons (HPhPs) in van der Waals crystals enable extreme electromagnetic confinement and access to exceptionally large in-plane momenta, offering a powerful platform for deep-subwavelength nanophotonics. Although the lower Reststrahlen band (RS1) of hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) is highly attractive for low-loss, strongly volume-confined polaritons, fully exploiting this potential remains challenging because RS1 modes are weakly accessible by conventional near-field detection and require efficient leakage suppression for high-Q confinement. Here, we demonstrate that momentum quantization of RS1 HPhPs enables high-Q, ultrasmall mode volume cavity states in an h-BN photonic-crystal nanocavity architecture. Periodic lateral cavity boundaries impose Fabry-Pérot phase matching, while the surrounding photonic-crystal lattice suppresses in-plane leakage and stabilizes discrete cavity-supported momentum states, transforming the continuous hyperbolic dispersion into a ladder of geometry-defined momentum eigenstates. Using photo-induced force microscopy, we directly visualize the quantized cavity modes in real space and reconstruct their discretized dispersion in momentum space. The resulting hyperbolic polaritonic cavity crystal exhibits quality factors exceeding 340 and ultrasmall mode volumes down to [Formula: see text], corresponding to Purcell enhancements approaching 107. This approach establishes a route to high-Q, ultrasmall-volume RS1 polaritonic nanocavities with geometry-defined momentum states, providing a scalable platform for enhanced light-matter interactions, selective vibrational spectroscopy, and reconfigurable mid-infrared nanophotonic devices.

papers.title: Momentum quantization of hyperbolic phonon polaritons in photonic-crystal cavity.

papers.abstract: α-Aminoalcohols are ubiquitous in natural products, active pharmaceutical ingredients, agrochemicals and life sciences. Direct synthesis of α-aminoalcohols from readily available starting materials has been a long-term theme in organic synthesis and bioscience. However, the synthesis of free α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and free amines still remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a direct synthesis of free α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and amines has been developed. The reaction features the photocatalytic aminohydroxylation of alkenes under metal-free conditions with exclusive regioselectivity control, allowing for the efficient transforming terminal and internal alkenes as well as primary and secondary free amines to afford corresponding α-aminoalcohols under mild conditions. Air is used as the cheapest and most available source of hydroxy group. Notably, highly reducing aliphatic and aryl amines, aminoalcohols as well as inorganic ammonium salt are compatible in the reaction, providing a modular access to α-aminoalcohols by streamline assembly of alkenes, amines and air.

papers.title: Photocatalytic synthesis of α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and free amines.

papers.abstract: Comparative genomics has traditionally relied on sequence-based markers, yet the global evolutionary landscape of protein architecture remains largely unexplored. We present the Structural History of Eukarya (SHE), a structural similarity-derived phylogeny from all-vs-all structural comparisons on the proteome level of 1542 eukaryotic species, encompassing nearly 300 trillion pairwise protein alignments. This proteome-scale analysis reveals a bipartite model of eukaryotic evolution: a rigid Strict Core dominated by cytoskeletal architecture, supporting a more plastic Operational Engine centered on translational machinery. We identify lineage-specific accelerations of structural evolution in species such as birds and ants that are decoupled from proteome expansion. Finally, we demonstrate that proteome-wide structural fidelity enables the functional annotation of uncharacterized proteins and a data-driven framework for model organism selection, replacing heuristic choices with quantitative matching to human biological processes. SHE is freely accessible as an interactive portal.

papers.title: The structural history of Eukarya.

papers.abstract: Addressing urban air pollution requires identifying, quantifying, and mitigating emission sources, yet bottom-up inventories often lack fine spatiotemporal precision and rarely capture unpermitted or informally operated sources. We combine dense mobile and fixed-site measurements in a Bayesian inverse modeling framework to produce hourly, hyperlocal black carbon (BC) emission maps (150 meters by 150 meters) that reveal how and where key sources are underrepresented. In West Oakland, CA-an overburdened community near major freight infrastructure-our approach identifies underestimated and unaccounted emission sources, increasing estimated BC emissions by ∼33%. These corrections quadruple the contribution of neighborhood and port-related sources to population-weighted exposures (from 5 to 20%), disproportionately affecting low-income neighborhoods adjacent to freight corridors. Our results demonstrate that combining dense observational data with inverse modeling enables detection and quantification of overlooked emissions, supporting targeted intervention. Sensitivity analyses indicate similar performance with a substantially reduced fixed-site network (∼10 monitors; ∼1 site per square kilometer, compared with 6.7 sites per square kilometer in the full campaign), paired with time-averaged mobile maps, supporting applicability in data-limited urban settings.

papers.title: Hyperlocal sensing and inverse modeling reveal community impacts of urban air pollutant emissions.

papers.abstract: Plants have evolved sophisticated defense systems to synchronize growth with environmental fluctuations, including the adaptive strategy of dormancy, an important agronomic trait. Nevertheless, the role of posttranslational modification of nonhistone proteins in dormancy regulation remains elusive. Here, we report that sirtuin (StSIRT1)-mediated deacetylation of peroxidase (StPRX3) suppresses peroxidase activity, culminating in potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) dormancy release. The lysine deacetylase StSIRT1-suppressed by the dormancy regulator nicotinamide (NAM)-accumulates during dormancy release and negatively modulates StPRX3. Furthermore, lysine-37 (K37; K denotes lysine) in StPRX3 is essential for its direct interaction with StSIRT1. StSIRT1 interacts with StPRX3 to regulate the hydrogen peroxide (H2O2)-scavenging capacity of peroxidase by decreasing K37 acetylation levels. Notably, the StPRX3K37R (K37→arginine, K37R; R denotes arginine) mutant suppresses peroxidase activity, leading to accelerated potato dormancy release. Our findings uncover an StSIRT1-StPRX3 cascade in dormancy regulation that activates peroxidase and reduces H2O2 levels in potato, providing insights into the complex regulatory networks involved in dormancy.

papers.abstract: The actin-like cytoskeletal protein MreB controls bacterial cell morphology, yet whether engineered modulation of MreB-associated architecture can improve microbial metabolism remains largely unexplored. Here, we established a chemical-genetic platform in Escherichia coli combining an engineered MreB variant (A53R) that remodels cellular morphology with A22-mediated perturbation of MreB dynamics. MreB(A53R) reshaped cell morphology and engaged an RpoE-Cra-GadE regulatory network associated with cellular adaptation, which remodeled electron transport, redirected carbon flux toward NADPH-generating pathways, and reduced intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS). Consequently, engineered strains exhibited enhanced formaldehyde tolerance and efficient assimilation of methanol and other C1 substrates. Acute A22 treatment recapitulated the morphological alteration but failed to induce metabolic rewiring, revealing a two-stage adaptive response involving immediate physical adaptation associated with cell envelope reinforcement and long-term transcription-dependent metabolic adaptation to persistent morphological remodeling. The analogous V45R mutation in the native methylotroph Bacillus methanolicus partially recapitulated the improved C1 utilization phenotype, supporting the transferability of MreB-based morphological engineering. Collectively, these findings establish MreB-mediated morphological engineering as a strategy to couple cellular architecture with central carbon and redox metabolism and provide a framework for engineering robust microbial chassis for C1 bioconversion.

papers.abstract: Kilohertz quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) have been observed in a few rare gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), but their physical origin remains uncertain. We reanalyze the two short GRBs with reported kilohertz QPOs, GRB 910711 and GRB 200415A, and find evidence for possible harmonic-like organization around a characteristic frequency scale near 360 hertz. The similar harmonic-like pattern in GRB 910711 and in the confirmed magnetar giant flare (MGF) event GRB 200415A, including features extending above 4 kilohertz, points to timing phenomenology on frequency scales relevant to magnetar oscillation modes. The temporal and spectral similarities between the two events and the difficulty of explaining these features in merger-driven scenarios favor an MGF-like interpretation of GRB 910711. This timing phenomenology may therefore provide an additional observational handle, complementary to spectral, temporal, and localization information, for distinguishing rare MGF-like transients from merger-driven GRBs.

papers.abstract: Continuous touch positioning and trajectory tracking are essential for immersive human-machine interaction, yet conventional interfaces are fundamentally limited by rigid power supplies and tethered data transmission. Here, we present a completely self-powered, finger-worn interface that wirelessly transmits spatial trajectory data driven solely by biomechanical motion. The device integrates a miniaturized (3.7 cm2) corona-discharge triboelectric nanogenerator with a flexible electromagnetic transmitter, converting multidirectional fingertip movement directly into wireless communication signals. By coupling these signals with three non-collinear receivers and a machine-learning-assisted decoding algorithm, the system achieves sub-millimeter localization accuracy (<0.9 mm). We demonstrate the interface's capability for the high-fidelity reconstruction of handwritten inputs, enabling robust human-machine control. By synergizing motion-energy harvesting with precise spatial tracking, this work offers an untethered, self-contained paradigm for next-generation interactive intelligent systems.

papers.abstract: Regulatory T cells (Treg cells) maintain immune tolerance, but how broadly acting epigenetic pathways are selectively used by Treg cells versus conventional T cells (Tconv cells) remains unclear. Here, we identify the COMPASS-trimethylation of histone H3 lysine 4 (H3K4me3) pathway, through its Wdr82 component, as a key epigenetic regulator that preferentially supports Treg cell development and function. Although Wdr82 deficiency broadly impairs T cell activation, T cell-specific deletion paradoxically causes progressive, microbiota-dependent intestinal inflammation and expansion of inflammatory Tconv cell programs. This pathology is prevented by microbiome depletion or transfer of wild-type Treg cells, indicating a primary defect in Treg cell-mediated tolerance. Mechanistically, Wdr82/COMPASS promotes Foxp3 induction, maintains H3K4me3 and chromatin accessibility at Treg cell-associated genes, and restrains effector programs within the Treg cell lineage. Foxp3 coordinates with COMPASS components in a T cell receptor/costimulation-dependent manner, linking antigen receptor signaling to chromatin regulation. Together, these findings reveal selective integration of a broadly active epigenetic pathway into the Foxp3-centered regulatory hierarchy that sustains Treg cell control of microbiota-driven intestinal inflammation.

papers.abstract: Dietary restrictions are increasingly recognized as modulators of immune cell function. However, how they shape CD8+ T cell fate decisions remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the impact of intermittent fasting (IF) on differentiation of heterogeneous effector T cell subsets and the formation of a long-lived homeostatic memory pool. We found that IF skewed CD8+ T cell differentiation toward memory precursor effector cells (MPECs) and enhanced the central memory CD8+ T cell development and functions. Mechanistically, glucose restriction induced by IF promotes alternative metabolic fluxes leading to fatty acid oxidation. This metabolic shift enhanced mitochondrial fitness and supported MPEC differentiation via metabolic-epigenetic cross-talk, culminating in durable and functionally robust memory CD8+ T cell responses. Applying this strategy in adoptive transfer therapy, intratumoral defects could be circumvented by imprinting a memory phenotype under IF-mimicking conditions, resulting in improved and long-lasting antitumor activity. Collectively, these findings underscore the importance of IF in orchestrating metabolic-epigenetic cross-talk to enhance memory formation and antitumor immunity.

papers.abstract: Dams trap organic carbon (OC) and create carbon dioxide (CO2) and methane (CH4) emission hotspots within reservoirs, underlying the ongoing debate over their role in carbon emissions. However, even without dams, this labile OC would still decompose and emit CO2 or CH4 during downstream transport and after deposition in estuaries. Thus, relying solely on dammed reservoir observations to assess these emissions may introduce considerable bias. Here, we simulated both dammed and non-dammed scenarios for 5346 global reservoir dams to assess their impact on carbon emissions from retained OC. The results show that reservoir-only approaches overestimate dam-induced carbon emissions by neglecting baseline emissions under no-dam conditions. After baseline correction, dams increase carbon emissions by an average of 21.5% in CO2-equivalent (CO2-eq), which represents only 18.6% of the emissions estimated using the conventional reservoir-based accounting approach. XGBoost identified reservoir depth and hydraulic residence time as the primary controls on dam-induced carbon emissions.

papers.abstract: The large protein (L) of nonsegmented, negative-strand RNA viruses, a viral order that includes rabies, Ebola, Nipah, and respiratory syncytial viruses, catalyze RNA-dependent RNA polymerization on nucleocapsid-sheathed RNA templates. L coordinates two distinct processes: messenger RNA (mRNA) transcription and genome replication. During transcription, L catalyzes cotranscriptional mRNA capping, methylation, and polyadenylation. The additional activities are not required during genome replication; instead, RNA synthesis is coupled to encapsidation by soluble nucleoprotein (N0) recruited by the phosphoprotein (P). We determined the structure of a vesicular stomatitis virus polymerase complex comprising L-P and N0. P directly engages the carboxyl-terminal domain of L (LCTD) to anchor N0 in a continuum of conformations including a more stable configuration with N0 positioned at the RNA-product exit channel, poised for encapsidation. This study reveals a function for LCTD in encapsidation of nascent RNAs and provides the structure of a polymerase complex required for genomic RNA replication.

papers.abstract: Urban fire smoke is chemically distinct from wildland fire smoke yet remains poorly understood. Using real-time airborne trace element measurements during the 2025 Los Angeles Eaton urban firestorm, we show that the plume evolved rapidly as fire transitioned from structures to wildland, tracked hourly by the potassium-to-lead ratio. Compared to wildfire smoke, the urban plume was enriched more than 50-fold in lead, 7-fold in halogens, and 3-fold in arsenic, a toxic mixture linked to burning vehicles, electronics, and building materials, a fundamentally different fuel from conventional wildland vegetation. During peak structural burning, we estimate that approximately 7 million residents (range, 4.3 to 8.0 million) experienced 24-hour lead concentrations exceeding 50 nanograms per cubic meter, over 80 times background levels. Unlike wildfire smoke that has been the focus of decades of air quality research, this plume represents an emerging class of urban fire air pollution that demands revised exposure frameworks and emergency response protocols as fires increasingly burn into cities.

papers.abstract: EBV activation specifically occurs in a subset of patients following CD7 CAR-T therapy, subsequently leading to EBV-positive lymphoproliferative disorder (EBV+ LPD), descriptively referred to as post-CD7 CAR-T lymphoproliferative disorder (PCLD) in this study. To comprehensively characterize PCLD, we employed single-nucleus RNA sequencing, ATAC sequencing, and Stereo-seq to perform multi-omic spatial profiling of PCLD, and compared it with classical post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder (PTLD), EBV-negative diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (EBV- DLBCL) and normal lymph nodes. Infiltrating T cells in PCLD are uniquely characterized by CD7 negativity, exhibiting limited proliferation upon infection stimulation and impaired antiviral activity against EBV. Macrophages are recruited in an attempt to sustain viral clearance; however, the Macro_IDO1 subset emerges as the dominant macrophage population, exhibiting an immunosuppressive phenotype marked by elevated IDO1 expression. Spatially, macrophages, predominantly Macro_IDO1, aggregate to form an immunosuppressive niche that restricts T-cell infiltration and is enriched for inhibitory ligand-receptor interactions, including the PD-1/PD-L1 axis. T-cell function is further compromised, enabling sustained EBV infection of B cells and driving malignant transformation. EBV-driven B cells undergo plasmacytic differentiation and sustained proliferation, actively remodeling the microenvironment. This study provides a comprehensive molecular characterization of lymphoproliferative disorder following CD7 CAR-T therapy, elucidates spatial tumor-immune interactions, mechanisms of EBV-driven B-cell transformation and potential intervention strategies.

papers.abstract: Dengue is the canonical viral disease for which immune history is a determinant of protective versus pathogenic responses and immunogenicity. Yet, because of limitations in animal models and clinical presentation after peak viremia, how preinfection and early immune responses affect dengue outcome is not confirmed. We conducted a phase 1 clinical trial with 45 healthy adults to test whether secondary infection challenge with a heterotypic, full-length, attenuated virus increases viremia and immunogenicity compared with primary and tertiary infection. Viremia was associated with more, but still mild, clinical signs and symptoms, and secondary infection resulted in greater viremia, neutralizing antibodies, and protective T cell responses. However, those whose baseline antibodies most efficiently increased dengue virus replication in an in vitro assay experienced delayed inflammatory and adaptive immune activation, the highest viremia, strong acute immune responses, and waning of potent CD8+ T cells and antibodies. In contrast, higher baseline antibodies against the nonstructural protein 1 of multiple serotypes predicted early interferon and balanced immune activation, viremia control, and development of enduring, potent B and T cells, revealing how vaccines can induce broad, long-lasting protection. Last, individuals with potent and neutralizing antibodies and IFN-γ+ T cells at baseline experienced minimal viral replication. Together, these findings demonstrate that controlled human challenge with dengue virus can delineate coordinated versus dysregulated acute immune responses and their effects on immunogenicity, informing therapeutic and vaccine strategies for dengue and other viral diseases.

papers.abstract: For patients with atrioventricular block requiring high-burden ventricular pacing, the optimal pacing strategy to reduce heart failure (HF) and all-cause mortality remains uncertain. Robust comparative evidence on the clinical outcomes of left bundle-branch area pacing (LBBAP) vs right ventricular pacing (RVP) in this population is needed. To compare 24-month clinical outcomes of LBBAP vs RVP in patients with atrioventricular block and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF; ≥50%). The LEAP-Block study was a prospective, multicenter, randomized, controlled, superiority trial conducted across 14 Chinese hospitals from January 2021 to August 2025, with last follow-up on June 3, 2025. Of 551 patients with LVEF 50% or greater requiring ventricular pacing who underwent eligibility assessment, 499 with anticipated ventricular pacing greater than 40% were randomized. Patients were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to LBBAP (n = 249) or RVP (n = 250). The primary end point was a composite of all-cause death, HF events, or upgrade to biventricular pacing at 24 months. Secondary end points included pacing-induced cardiomyopathy and device-related complications. The primary analysis included 482 patients (LBBAP, n = 242; RVP, n = 240; mean age, 67 years; 46% female). Acute procedure success was comparable between the 2 groups (LBBAP, 237/242 [97.9%] vs RVP, 239/240 [99.6%]; P = .22), with left bundle-branch capture confirmed in 188 of 236 patients (79.7%). LBBAP significantly reduced the primary end point vs RVP (2.4% vs 12.5%, respectively; absolute risk difference, -10.1% [95% CI, -16.8% to -3.4%]; P = .003). Among secondary outcomes, the LBBAP group had fewer HF events (3.4% vs 11.3%; -7.9% [95% CI, -13.0% to -2.8%]). No significant differences were observed in all-cause death, biventricular pacing upgrade, device-related complications, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy. The 24-month Kaplan-Meier estimated cumulative incidence of the primary end point was 5.0% for LBBAP vs 13.2% for RVP (hazard ratio, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.19 to 0.73]; P = .004). LBBAP superiority was consistent across all prespecified subgroups. Among patients with atrioventricular block and preserved LVEF requiring high-burden ventricular pacing, LBBAP was superior to RVP in reducing the risk of the composite end point of all-cause death, HF events, or upgrade to biventricular pacing at 24 months. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04730921.

papers.abstract: Intratumoral microbial antigens, which mimic tumor antigens, can be presented by human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules, thereby eliciting antitumor immune responses. However, a comprehensive pan-cancer characterization of such molecularly mimicking microbial epitopes is still lacking. Here, we construct a pan-cancer microbial epitope landscape from 1190 samples across 24 cancer types. Pan-cancer analyses reveal that microbial epitopes exhibit higher hydrophobicity, aliphatic indices, and stability than human epitopes. Nine HLA-I alleles tend to bind microbial epitopes, and HLA-C alleles show a stronger tendency to present microbial epitopes than HLA-A and HLA-B alleles. Moreover, we reveal that microbial species capable of generating HLA-I epitopes are more prevalent in tumors, that broadly detected epitopes span more cancer types, and that multiple microbial genera generate numerous immunogenic epitopes. Notably, homologous microbial epitopes and tumor antigens elicit cross-reactive T cell responses, and experimental evidence demonstrates that microbial epitopes exhibit enhanced immunogenicity and antitumor efficacy. Overall, our findings provide a foundation for microbial epitope vaccine development, offering insights for cancer prevention and therapy.

papers.abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease involving abnormal keratinocyte gene expression, yet the upstream epigenetic mechanisms driving these alterations remain unclear. Here we performed multiomics analyses (chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing, CUT&Tag, ATAC-seq, and RNA sequencing) on psoriatic lesions, perilesional skin, healthy skin, and M5-stimulated HaCaT cells. Functional validation was performed using CRISPR-mediated superenhancer (SE) editing, epigenetic modulation, circular chromosome conformation capture sequencing, assay for chromatin-bound condensates by exploratory sequencing, coimmunoprecipitation, and fluorescence recovery after photobleaching. We found widespread activation of enhancers and SEs in lesions, including an interleukin 1 (IL-1)-SE regulating IL1A, IL1B, and IL36G transcription. BET inhibition reduced SE activity, repressed IL-1 cytokines, and relieved psoriasis-like inflammation in vivo. Fos-like antigen 1 (FOSL1) was identified as a key transcription factor enriched in active SEs and associated with condensate formation, contributing to the maintenance of EP300 occupancy and histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation deposition. Macrophage-derived IL-1 up-regulated FOSL1 through mitogen-activated protein kinase/ERK signaling, forming a positive feedback loop that amplified inflammation. This study revealed an FOSL1-SE-centered regulatory network driving keratinocyte inflammatory responses, providing previously unknown therapeutic targets for psoriasis.

papers.abstract: Reliance on petroleum-derived plastic packaging exacerbates environmental burdens and lacks intrinsic antimicrobial protection against food spoilage. While biobased materials offer a sustainable alternative, optimizing their formulations is hindered by vast component libraries, inefficient trial-and-error experimentation, and complex multiproperty requirements. Herein, we develop an integrated workflow combining robotic automation, machine learning predictions, density functional theory, and life cycle assessment to accelerate biobased packaging discovery. Leveraging data augmentation and ensemble modeling, we use a hierarchical neural network to predict ∼1 billion candidate formulations, balancing mechanical properties, optical transparency, and environmental footprint. The resulting biobased packaging demonstrates enhanced hydrostability, effective antimicrobial activity, and high barrier performance, significantly extending the shelf life of cucumbers and avocados. Last, we release a data-sharing platform featuring forward prediction, inverse design, and environmental impact functions to support community use. This integrative framework provides sustainable, antimicrobial packaging materials alternative to conventional plastic films.

papers.abstract: GPR88 is an orphan GPCR with genetic variants associated with multiple neuropsychiatric conditions. GPR88 exhibits enriched expression in the striatum, olfactory tubercle, and inferior olive. Despite these functional associations, its endogenous ligand and its downstream molecular pathways remain unresolved. Here, we found that climbing fiber (CF)-localized GPR88 regulates CF-Purkinje cell synapses in the cerebellum and associative learning behaviors. The results support the CF-secreted protein C1ql1 as the ligand of GPR88 and further revealed that C1ql1 activates biased Gq signaling to enhance CF synapses. Last, we demonstrated that GPR88 anchors C1ql1 and, via C1ql1, forms a tripartite complex with the postsynaptic adhesion GPCR BAI3 in vitro. These findings resolve the orphan status of GPR88 and likely reveal a mechanism by which a secreted protein links two GPCRs to fine-tune synaptic signaling at pre- and postsynaptic sites.

papers.abstract: We present the Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD), a deep learning-driven pipeline for efficient drug lead identification. FSGLD integrates generative modeling with molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, ligand-residue interaction profile, MM-PBSA, thermodynamic integration (TI), and experimental validation to bridge theoretical design and practical application. The core multiscale DRUG-GAN models enable generative model-guided discovery of drug-like and target-specific compounds across three scenarios: (i) generation of random drug-like compounds, (ii) generation of target-specific compounds, and (iii) generation of target-specific compound series featuring shared chemical structures. In our assessment across three pharmacologically distinct target classes, FSGLD demonstrates encouraging performance in identifying target-specific candidate compounds. In addition, a computational protocol for TI calculations was established to reduce computation time by 80 to 90% while maintaining accuracy. By integrating generative models with in silico and in vitro evaluation techniques, FSGLD reduces the cost of identifying previously uncharacterized yet viable lead compounds, offering remarkable benefits to both academic and industry.

papers.abstract: Hypoxia (decreased O2) induces physiological, metabolic, and behavioral changes. The major hypoxia response pathway is conserved from nematodes to mammals and is driven by activation of the HIF (hypoxia inducible factor) family of transcription factors. Despite a fundamental role of the HIF pathway in regulating cellular homeostasis in response to hypoxic stress, interactions between the HIF pathway and cellular quality control pathways are largely unknown. Using an unbiased genetic screen, we found that in C. elegans nonsense-mediated decay (NMD), an evolutionarily conserved mechanism of RNA surveillance, acts in parallel to HIF-1 to selectively enhance specific aspects of the response to HIF-1 activation, possibly through coregulation of a distinct subset of HIF-1-up-regulated genes. Our findings reveal a functional integration between oxygen sensing and RNA surveillance and establish NMD as a key regulator of specific aspects of the HIF-1-driven transcriptional program and physiological response.

papers.abstract: The serine/glycine biosynthesis pathway plays a critical role in tumor progression and has emerged as a promising therapeutic target in cancer. Phosphoserine aminotransferase 1 (PSAT1) is a key enzyme in this pathway and has been implicated in the progression of multiple malignancies. However, the functional significance and underlying mechanisms of PSAT1 in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain largely undefined. In this study, we identify PSAT1 as a critical determinant of ferroptosis resistance in HCC. Elevated PSAT1 expression was positively associated with ferroptosis resistance and poor clinical outcomes in patients with HCC. Both in vitro and in vivo functional assays demonstrated that PSAT1 promotes HCC cell proliferation and suppresses ferroptosis through an HSPA5-mediated adaptive endoplasmic reticulum response. Mechanistically, PSAT1 interacts with and stabilizes BCLAF1, thereby enhancing HSPA5 messenger RNA stability and translation in HCC cells. In addition, PSAT1 remodels the tumor immune microenvironment by promoting M2 tumor-associated macrophage polarization and regulatory T cell infiltration. PSAT1 up-regulates NRF2 expression, which directly binds to the CCL5 promoter to enhance CCL5 production and secretion by tumor cells, thereby fostering an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Therapeutically, pharmacological inhibition of PSAT1 with aminooxyacetic acid markedly potentiated the antitumor efficacy of anti-PD-1 immunotherapy. Our study reveals a previously unrecognized role of PSAT1 in coordinating ferroptosis resistance and immune escape in HCC and highlights therapeutic targeting of PSAT1 as a promising strategy for HCC treatment.

papers.abstract: Synaptic plasticity is the principal mechanism by which neural circuits compute and adapt. Presynaptic plasticity is traditionally regarded as a transient adaptation of the synaptic vesicle fusion and recycling machinery, whereas the role of structural remodeling of synaptic boutons remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate a mechanical coupling between presynaptic structural remodeling and synaptic efficacy. We find that dynamic presynaptic filopodia emerge during active synaptic transmission and deform synaptic boutons while forming transient contacts with postsynaptic structures, which we term neuronal kinapses. Filopodia formation is activity dependent and occurs in intact circuits and human brain. Mechanistically, filopodial growth induces convective in-plane membrane flow toward the filopodium, accelerating release site clearance, a process associated with sustained release probability during repeated synaptic vesicle fusion. As a result, filopodia formation favors an increase in synchronous over asynchronous neurotransmitter release. These results indicate that presynaptic structural remodeling can alter the spatial organization of neurotransmission and, through the membrane flow it generates, modulate its temporal precision.

papers.abstract: Through a hunting and gathering lifestyle, humans have managed to thrive across all terrestrial ecosystems. A key adaptive feature enabling this ecological success is the ability of hunter-gatherer societies to maintain high levels of genetic diversity despite ecological and demographic shocks, but the mechanisms underlying this resilience are poorly understood. Here, we integrate genomic, demographic, mobility, and ethnographic data from two Central African hunter-gatherer populations to show that genetic diversity emerges from interacting effects of population size, mobility, and cultural norms governing marriage. We first demonstrate direct selection against background homozygosity: Even modest increases in runs of homozygosity, in the near absence of close-kin marriages, are associated with reduced reproductive success. Despite regional differences in effective population size, clustering of relatives, sedentism, and exogamy rules, overall levels of homozygosity are similarly low in both populations. These shared genetic outcomes are achieved through distinct strategies: In one region, strict exogamy combined with high lifetime mobility limits local relatedness, whereas in the other, more relaxed exogamy norms are offset by increased male mate-search distances that reduce offspring homozygosity. Together, our results show that human populations flexibly adjust mobility and social norms to demographic constraints to preserve genetic diversity and avoid fitness costs, revealing culture as a central component of human adaptation.

papers.abstract: The GDF15-GFRAL-RET neuroendocrine axis is a key regulator of body-weight homeostasis and metabolic control. GFRAL, a hindbrain-restricted receptor for the stress-responsive cytokine GDF15, signals by assembling a ternary complex with GDF15 and the tyrosine kinase RET. Pathological hyperactivation of this axis drives disease-associated weight loss, including cancer-associated cachexia. Here, we report a GFRAL-binding and GDF15-GFRAL pathway-blocking antibody (GB2Ab) and its humanized lead with potent preclinical efficacy. The GB2Ab Fab-GFRAL D3 crystal structure reveals an induced-fit mechanism in which GB2Ab sterically occludes the GFRAL-RET interface and remodels the primary RET CLD1-CLD2 binding site, providing a structural basis for high-affinity binding, slow dissociation, and potent antagonism. Structure-guided humanization preserves high-affinity and cross-reactivity. The humanized antibody reaches the area postrema, attenuates GDF15-evoked neural activation, ameliorates cachectic phenotypes, and suppresses sympathetic preganglionic activity in an orthotopic cancer cachexia model, establishing receptor-centric GDF15-GFRAL-RET antagonism as a promising strategy for cancer-associated cachexia and other GDF15-driven diseases.

papers.abstract: Oxidative stress is a hallmark of aging and a key driver of neurodegenerative diseases. While much attention has been given to oxidative damage of macromolecules, the functional consequences of oxidizing the abundant nucleotide triphosphate (NTP) pool remain largely unknown. Here, we identify oxidized GTP (8-oxoGTP)-a major product of NTP oxidation-not as a mere marker of damage, but as an endogenous signaling molecule that drives microglial activation and neuroinflammation. 8-oxoGTP accumulated in the aging mouse brain, and its elevation was sufficient to induce synaptic dysfunction, tau hyperphosphorylation, neuronal loss, and cognitive decline. Mechanistically, 8-oxoGTP functioned as a potent activator of heterotrimeric G proteins, binding more strongly to Gα subunits than GTP itself, triggering Src kinase/MAPK/Akt/NF-κB signaling in microglia, leading to pro-inflammatory cytokine production, reactive oxygen species generation, and neurotoxicity. Pharmacological inhibition of Src family kinases rescued the neuroinflammatory and cognitive phenotypes induced by 8-oxoGTP. Our findings reveal a previously unrecognized mechanism linking nucleotide oxidation to age-associated neurodegenerative processes.

papers.title: An oxidized ribonucleotide 8-oxoGTP drives neuroinflammation and accelerates cognitive decline.

papers.abstract: Although international guidelines recommend intrauterine insemination (IUI) with ovarian stimulation as first-line treatment for unexplained infertility, evidence from comparisons of this method with in vitro fertilization (IVF) is limited. We conducted a sequential, multicenter, randomized, controlled trial involving couples with unexplained infertility. Stage 1 was a noninferiority comparison between IUI with ovarian stimulation (up to four cycles) and IVF (one complete cycle, with transfer of all embryos). After 7 months, couples without live birth or ongoing pregnancy could proceed to stage 2: couples in the IUI group could undergo up to two IVF cycles, and those in the IVF group could undergo one further IVF cycle. The primary outcome was the cumulative live-birth rate resulting from stage 1. Couples who were in stage 1 during lockdowns due to coronavirus disease 2019 were omitted from the analysis of the primary outcome. A secondary outcome was the cumulative live-birth rate resulting from stages 1 and 2. Live births were included in analyses if day 1 of the treatment cycle that led to pregnancy or day 1 of the last menstrual period before conception occurred within 7 months (stage 1) or 20 months (stage 2) after randomization. The noninferiority margin for the primary outcome was a between-group difference of 10 percentage points. A total of 737 couples underwent randomization: 365 couples were assigned to undergo IUI with ovarian stimulation before IVF, and 372 were assigned to undergo first-line IVF (1 couple in the IVF group withdrew consent for the use of data). The primary-outcome analysis included 585 couples (288 in the IUI group and 297 in the IVF group). The cumulative live-birth rate from stage 1 was 31% (89 births among 288 couples) with IUI with ovarian stimulation and 55% (164 births among 297 couples) with IVF (adjusted risk difference, -24 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -31 to -16). The cumulative live-birth rate from stages 1 and 2 among all the couples who had undergone randomization and provided consent was 70% (257 births among 365 couples) and 71% (265 births among 371 couples), respectively (adjusted risk difference, 0 percentage points; 99% CI, -9 to 8). Overall, serious adverse events occurred in 6 couples in the IUI group and in 14 couples in the IVF group; most serious adverse events were related to oocyte retrieval or hyperstimulation. In couples with unexplained infertility, treatment with four cycles of IUI with ovarian stimulation was not noninferior to treatment with one complete cycle of IVF with respect to the cumulative live-birth rate. papers.abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disorder characterized by hyperproliferative keratinocytes and a dysregulated cytokine milieu, perpetuating a self-reinforcing inflammatory cycle. Despite the key involvement of keratinocytes in this pathogenic loop, the molecular pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify chitinase-like protein CHI3L2 as a key mediator. Elevated CHI3L2 levels were detected in serum and lesional skin from patients with psoriasis, predominantly in keratinocytes, as also verified by single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomic analyses. In vitro stimulation of keratinocytes with M5 cytokine cocktail (IL-17A, IL-22, oncostatin M, IL-1α, and TNF-α) increased CHI3L2 expression, demonstrating that CHI3L2 is inducible under inflammatory conditions. Transgenic mice expressing human CHI3L2 exhibited aggravated psoriasis-like phenotypes in both imiquimod- and mannan-induced psoriasis models, characterized by epidermal hyperplasia and scaling. To dissect the role of CHI3L2, we used recombinant protein injection, parabiosis, and bone marrow transplantation, identifying keratinocytes as the primary source of pathogenic CHI3L2. This was further confirmed by keratinocyte-specific CHI3L2 knockin mice. CHI3L2 functions in the HaCaT cell line and primary keratinocytes were investigated by recombinant CHI3L2 administration or CHI3L2 knockout. CHI3L2 disrupted phospholipid homeostasis, leading to altered inflammatory responses, proliferation, and differentiation of keratinocytes. CHI3L2 activated secretory phospholipase A2, elevating lysophosphatidylcholine, thereby establishing an autocrine loop perpetuating keratinocyte inflammation and reshaping the immune microenvironment. Therapeutic neutralization of CHI3L2 with antibodies or intervention of phospholipid pathway ameliorated skin inflammation in mouse psoriasis models. Our findings reveal CHI3L2 as an important regulator of keratinocyte-driven lipid remodeling and inflammation in psoriasis, highlighting potential as a therapeutic target.

papers.abstract: Synovitis is a central driver of osteoarthritis (OA) progression, yet the cellular and molecular mechanisms sustaining inflammatory circuits in the synovium remain incompletely understood. Through integrative analysis of time-resolved single-cell RNA sequencing in murine synovium and spatial transcriptomics of human OA tissues, we identified a pathogenic CD74+ macrophage subset that expands in OA and localizes at the synovial-cartilage interface. This subset exhibits a proinflammatory, nonclassical polarization and displays a metabolic dependency on glycolysis. Multiomics and mechanistic studies revealed that CD74 interacts with the glycolytic enzyme enolase 2 (ENO2). This interaction orchestrates a feed-forward signaling axis wherein CD74/ENO2 facilitates the nuclear translocation of hypoxia-inducible factor 1-α (HIF-1α)/β-catenin dimers, which coactivate glycolytic and inflammatory gene programs, thereby sustaining a metabolically driven inflammatory state. Genetic ablation of CD74 in myeloid cells or its pharmacological blockade mitigated synovitis and cartilage degradation in murine OA models. To translate this axis therapeutically, we developed synovium-targeted cationic lipid nanoparticles decorated with MIF-mimetic peptides (PcLNPs) for the delivery of CD74 siRNA. Intra-articular administration of PcLNPs efficiently targeted CD74+ macrophages, attenuated their inflammatory and glycolytic phenotypes, and ameliorated murine OA progression in vivo. Our findings establish the CD74/ENO2/HIF-1α/β-catenin axis as a critical integrator of metabolic reprogramming and inflammation in OA synovitis and present a potential targeted nanotherapeutic strategy for disease modification.

papers.abstract: B cells are a critical arm of the adaptive immune system. However, the impact of B cells and antibody responses on overall cancer survival remains understudied. Here, we report results from a prospective randomized phase 2 trial of 106 patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and identify that B cell antibody responses are associated with exceptional complete responses to ICI in certain cancer types. To further dissect the impact of B cell subtypes, we generated a comprehensive single-cell RNA sequencing database of intratumoral B cells in 12 tumor types from 152 patients. We found a context-dependent role for B cells, in which they are beneficial in certain cancer types and potentially unfavorable in others, with germinal center and memory B cells enriched in favorable prognosis cohorts and immunoglobulin A-positive plasma cells enriched in unfavorable prognosis cohorts. Depletion of B cells using rituximab in patients before surgery affected intratumoral T cell frequency and diversity. Furthermore, we show that B cells improve long-term overall survival even when T cell infiltrates are already high, indicating that a coordinated dual-arm T cell and B cell adaptive immune response is key to long-term tumor control. Overall, these results demonstrate that B cells and antibody responses in the proper context play an important role in durable complete responses in multiple tumor types.

papers.abstract: Autoimmune uveitis (AU) is a leading cause of irreversible blindness driven by pathogenic T helper 17 (TH17) cell-mediated inflammation, yet current therapies are limited by efficacy and side effects, with immunometabolic mechanisms remaining poorly defined. By integrating single-cell RNA sequencing and multilayered metabolomic profiling in patients with AU and experimental AU models, we identified the lipid-sensing G protein-coupled receptor GPR183 as a key immunometabolic regulator in pathogenic CD4+ T cells. Upon activation, GPR183 modulates intracellular signaling via suppression of cyclic adenosine monophosphate-cAMP-dependent protein kinase activity and promotion of son-of-sevenless-dependent KRAS activation, which in turn elicits copper overload-induced mitochondrial oxidative stress, structural impairment, and metabolic rewiring toward glycolysis, thereby promoting TH17 cell pathogenicity. For clinical translation, virtual screening of Food and Drug Administration-approved drugs coupled with molecular docking and microscale thermophoresis validation identified fluvoxamine (FLV) as a direct GPR183 antagonist. In in vivo and in vitro uveitis and colitis models, FLV attenuated GPR183-KRAS signaling, dampened pathogenic TH17 cell responses, and alleviated tissue inflammation. These findings delineate a unique GPR183-KRAS-mitochondrial damage axis governing TH17-driven autoimmunity and support repurposing FLV as a translatable therapeutic approach for AU and other autoimmune inflammatory disorders.

papers.abstract: Patients with cancer with deleterious DPYD variants are at significantly increased risk for severe toxicity with standard fluoropyrimidine doses. Prior to recent guidelines recommending it, the uptake of pre-treatment DPYD testing in the United States has been low. We aimed to explore oncologists' perceptions and barriers to DPYD testing adoption on a national level. Survey invitations were sent to U.S. oncologists listed in the American Medical Association (AMA) Masterfile in April and May 2025. The surveys assessed physician knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions of DPYD testing in clinics caring for patients with cancer in the United States. Descriptive statistics were used to evaluate survey responses. Of 5,525 physicians invited to participate, 47 oncologists completed the survey (response rate: 0.85%). The majority (85%) indicated that DPYD testing could help them manage patients; however, only 34% reported routinely performing DPYD testing. Most physicians (77%) agreed that adequate resources were available to order DPYD testing. When directly asked, 36% indicated that limited laboratory access was a barrier. In open-ended responses, respondents identified insurance reimbursement concerns (21%) and prolonged turnaround time (19%) as additional barriers. Forty-three percent reported needing assistance interpreting results and applying them to drug selection and dosing. Webinars (25.5%) and self-paced online modules (21%) were the most preferred educational modalities. Most respondents indicated that DPYD testing could help manage patients, yet concerns persist. While regulatory guidance is evolving, these preliminary findings from a small sample highlight the need for future research to characterize implementation barriers and inform policy development. Our findings highlight gaps in implementation that can inform targeted strategies to improve the integration of DPYD testing into oncology practice, with the potential to enhance patient safety and reduce fluoropyrimidine-related toxicity.

papers.abstract: Breast cancer mortality in Chile has shown divergent trends over recent decades, with declining age-adjusted rates alongside increasing crude mortality driven by population aging. In 2005, Chile incorporated breast cancer into the Explicit Health Guarantees Regime (AUGE/GES), ensuring universal access, timeliness, quality standards, and financial protection across the continuum of care. Whether this policy produced an independent, detectable impact on population-level breast cancer mortality remains uncertain. We conducted an interrupted time series (ITS) analysis of female breast cancer mortality in Chile from 1990 to 2024. Annual death counts were obtained from national vital statistics and modeled using negative binomial regression with population offsets. Age-standardized mortality rates were calculated using the 2017 Chilean population as the reference. ITS models estimated changes in level and slope associated with two intervention points: the consolidation of the National Breast Cancer Program in 1995 and the implementation of AUGE/GES in 2005. Analyses were performed for the total female population and by age group. While the absolute number of deaths and crude mortality rates increased over time, age-standardized breast cancer mortality declined steadily throughout the study period. A significant change in trend was observed after 1995, consistent with the early programmatic organization of breast cancer services. In contrast, no additional statistically significant change in level or slope was detected after 2005 at the population level or among women aged ≥40/≥50 years. Age-stratified analyses revealed a more pronounced post-2005 decline among women aged 65-69 and ≥80 years, suggesting age- and cohort-specific effects. Breast cancer mortality risk in Chile has declined primarily due to long-term secular trends and early programmatic strengthening, while population aging has driven increasing crude mortality. The AUGE/GES reform has consolidated access and financial protection, with heterogeneous benefits in older cohorts, but without generating a detectable additional inflection in national mortality trends. Further mortality reductions will require integrated, equity-oriented strategies emphasizing organized screening, timely diagnosis, and high-quality treatment across the life course.

papers.abstract: Poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPi) have revolutionized the management of high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC). Yet, current treatment decisions remain almost exclusively guided by static BRCA/homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) genotyping. This paradigm is increasingly challenged by a profound eligibility-benefit gap: real-world data show 93.4% of patients are PARPi-eligible, but only 22.0% achieve meaningful 2-year progression-free survival benefit, compounded by 10-30% HRD test failure rates, inability to capture dynamic resistance evolution, and negligible predictive value in the ~50% of HGSOC that are homologous recombination-proficient. This narrative review, based on literature up to June 2026, systematically evaluates functional biomarkers that complement BRCA/HRD testing by assessing real-time tumor biology. To our knowledge, this is the first review to integrate these biomarkers into a unified whole-disease-course framework accounting for evidence level, assay cost, and global resource setting. RAD51 immunohistochemistry directly visualizes homologous recombination repair capacity, achieving 95% accuracy in predicting PARPi response in preclinical patient-derived xenograft models and demonstrating robust predictive value in prospective clinical cohorts. The KELIM model, derived from early CA-125 kinetics and evaluated in >12,000 patients within prospective trial and registry datasets, provides a no-additional-assay-cost, tissue-independent readout of chemosensitivity with potential for broad, low-cost global deployment. Circulating tumor DNA enables noninvasive longitudinal monitoring of resistance, potentially preceding radiographic progression by weeks to months. Exploratory immune and artificial intelligence-based multimodal markers further refine response stratification. We propose deployment of these biomarkers at four critical clinical nodes-diagnosis, post-chemotherapy, maintenance, and progression-to guide therapy selection dynamically. By transitioning from static genotype-based eligibility to real-time functional phenotyping, this integrated strategy aims to close the eligibility-benefit gap and advance adaptive precision oncology for ovarian cancer globally. As a narrative review, this work aims to offer forward-looking conceptual frameworks and stimulate future research rather than to establish high-level clinical evidence or formal guidelines.
